newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korean President stalls on graft apology.
newsitem.headline: South Korean President stalls on graft apology.

text.p: South Korean President Kim Young-sam on Wednesday kept the country guessing whether he would apologise over his son's arrest for bribery and address allegations of foul play linked to his 1992 election campaign.
A presidential Blue House aide ruled out any statement on Wednesday, dashing widespread expectations, and said it was not clear whether any apology would be forthcoming.
"He will be making no statement today, and I cannot confirm any plans for an apology," said the official, who declined to be identified.
Kim's second son, Kim Hyun-chul, was arrested on Saturday on charges of accepting kickbacks worth millions of dollars and evading taxes.
The arrest followed a prosecution inquiry into corruption among politicians, government officials and bankers following the collapse of Hanbo Steel Co in January.

Opposition parties have alleged that Hanbo founder Chung Tae-soo helped bankroll the president's election win, and that Kim Hyun-chul laundered huge sums of leftover funds through his business cronies.
The Chosun Ilbo, South Korea's leading newspaper, said on Wednesday some of Kim's aides questioned the need for an apology.
"Even if he 'confesses' he will not be able to reveal the whole truth causing continuous pressure from the opposition and the people to reveal everything," the paper said.
